title: Large Language Models
summary: Making computation in large models more useful, stable, and deployable — not just larger.
argument: The central problem in large language models is not scale. It is waste. Most computation in a forward pass of a large model does not materially improve its output. Parameters are activated that contribute nothing. Training configurations produce instabilities that cost days of compute to diagnose. Inference pipelines stall under throughput pressure in ways that were entirely predictable.

Neryva's LLM program treats these as engineering problems — problems with measurable causes and improvable solutions. We study how models allocate computation, how training dynamics behave at scale, and how inference systems can be built to handle real operating conditions rather than benchmark assumptions.

threads.title: MoE Routing & Expert Selection
threads.question: How should routing objectives balance expert specialization against training stability when load imbalance is unavoidable at scale?

threads.title: Sparse Computation
threads.question: Which sparsity patterns preserve useful model behavior when memory budgets and latency targets are enforced at deployment time?

threads.title: Training Stability
threads.question: What early signals — measurable within the first 10% of training — reliably predict whether a configuration will diverge at larger scale?

threads.title: Inference Optimization
threads.question: How can serving pipelines adapt dynamically to workload variance without sacrificing throughput, quality, or latency guarantees?

currentWork: Literature review and problem formulation across all four threads. Initial experiments scoping routing objective design are underway — specifically, the interaction between auxiliary load-balancing loss terms and training loss stability in small-scale MoE runs.
futureDirection: Developing co-optimization strategies for routing and sparsity decisions during training, with the goal of reducing the instability introduced when both are tuned simultaneously.

literature.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
literature.annotation: The foundational paper introducing trainable gating for expert selection. Still the clearest statement of what routing is trying to solve.

literature.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
literature.annotation: Simplified routing that demonstrated the practical scaling benefits of sparse expert models. Essential reading on load balancing objectives.

literature.title: Efficient Large Scale Language Modeling with Mixtures of Experts
literature.annotation: Practical engineering of MoE training at scale. The most grounded analysis of routing strategies in a production-adjacent setting.
